evidence.excerpt: Returns. Last holiday season. Buy online, return in store.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Trigger of the evaluation: holiday returns across channels.

evidence.excerpt: The store couldn't see the online order, so staff were refunding to gift cards or telling people to mail it back.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Concrete operational failure in store returns.

evidence.excerpt: they'd just launched a loyalty program that was supposed to work everywhere and didn't, because store and web were two different customer records.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Loyalty program failed due to split customer records.

evidence.excerpt: Their COO, Angela, apparently stood in a store on December 27th watching the returns queue.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Hedged with 'apparently'; secondhand company lore, not observed by rep.

evidence.excerpt: That's the story everybody there tells.
evidence.label: opinion
evidence.speaker: Tom

evidence.excerpt: We proposed six hundred K a year. Stores and online together, one contract.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Deal size and structure proposed.

evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Initial claim of decider; later contradicted.

evidence.excerpt: they came in with a retail team, people who'd done store rollouts
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Raj
evidence.note: Raj's secondhand account of the competitor; rep wasn't there and relays in indirect speech.

evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: I wasn't there.

evidence.label: fact

evidence.label: fact

evidence.excerpt: Reaction: the online checkout demo. Their ecommerce lead loved it.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Online checkout demo drew positive reaction.

evidence.excerpt: Silence: the unified commerce part.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Unified commerce pitch got no reaction.

evidence.excerpt: Online and in-store on one platform, the line between them has pretty much disappeared.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Our slide wording on unified commerce.

evidence.excerpt: "that's a diagram."
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Bev
evidence.note: Bev dismissed the unified commerce slide.

evidence.excerpt: Then she asked how a return works. Step by step. At the till.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Bev wanted a concrete return walkthrough.

evidence.excerpt: I described it.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Rep described rather than demonstrated the return; terse answer.

evidence.excerpt: Nobody on our side had run a store rollout.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Our team lacked store rollout experience.

evidence.excerpt: They had six people from store operations.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Tom
evidence.note: Customer brought six store ops people to the workshop; we brought two.

evidence.label: fact

evidence.note: Partner-install answer met with silence; the moment the deal was lost.

evidence.excerpt: I knew on the drive home.
evidence.label: opinion

contradictions.what: Rep named CTO Raj as final decider, then said Angela signed with Adyen and 'probably Angela' made the call.
Rep said Raj was contact the whole way, but the actual signer Angela was met only once, at kickoff.
Rep said 'we were ahead' just before the workshop, yet the transcript shows rising store questions and gaps; rep knew it was lost at the workshop.
Raj reportedly wanted us and said we were ahead, yet Angela signed with the competitor.
Our pitch used 'unified commerce' and 'line has disappeared', but customer never used the term and met it with silence.

dodges.question: What did you say? (when Bev asked how a return works)
dodges.what: Answered tersely 'I described it', which later reveals no live demo was shown.

dodges.question: Who made the final call, and how do you know?
dodges.what: Answered confidently with Raj with no basis, then reversed under follow-up to 'Probably Angela'.
